title: Permute Keyed Modules Using a Buffer Socket
context: AI cluster compute blades and switch fabrics require frequent re-racking of keyed accelerator and transceiver modules where slots are tightly constrained and modules cannot be rested unsupported. Bimanual permutation through a single spare buffer socket verifies essential autonomous datacentre servicing skills.
instruction: Move the mis-racked modules between sockets—using the empty fourth socket as a buffer—so each module's coloured band matches its socket lamp disc, then press the white COMMIT button on the left controller box.
setup: Rigid 8.0 kg aluminium-and-steel bus strip with four keyed sockets in a row at pitch 70 mm (mouths at x = 0.240 m, y = -0.260, -0.190, -0.120, -0.050 m). Sockets 1-3 each feature a 20 mm coloured lamp disc on top (red, green, blue) specifying target module assignment; socket 4 has no lamp disc (empty buffer socket). Three 80 g keyed plug modules (45 x 18 x 28 mm housing, 28 x 16 x 18 mm steel nose with key rib and detent groove, 1.0 mm clearance per side) start seated in sockets 1-3 with sockets 1 and 2 swapped: socket 1 holds green module, socket 2 holds red module, socket 3 holds blue module. A controller box on the left at (0.280, 0.150 m) provides a white COMMIT button (36x36x12 mm cap, 8 mm travel to stop, 100 N/m spring) and a 50 mm diameter STATUS lamp (green when all 3 coloured sockets hold matching modules and no module is displaced; red otherwise).
scoring: Partial credit ladder: 0.25 when any module is pulled out (insertion depth < 16 mm); 0.50 when one mis-racked module is seated in its matching socket (depth >= 16 mm, lateral offset <= 1.5 mm, tilt <= 10 deg); 0.75 when both mis-racked modules are seated in their matching sockets; 1.00 when all three coloured sockets hold matching modules, COMMIT is pressed while STATUS is green, both grippers are open, and all bodies remain still (linear velocity <= 0.005 m/s, angular velocity <= 0.2 rad/s) for 1.0 s (20 steps). Zero-gate: fixture displacement > 5 mm, fixture tilt > 5 degrees, or any module dropped > 20 cm below the table top latches score 0.0.
reset_notes: Seat green module in socket 1, red module in socket 2, and blue module in socket 3 until each nose clicks past its spring plunger detent. Verify socket 4 is empty, COMMIT button cap is resting at top stop (+8 mm), and the controller box is securely fastened to the station table.
fidelity: Rigid 8 kg aluminium bus strip with 4 keyed sockets (pitch 70 mm, 1 mm clearance) and three 80 g plug modules with spring plunger latches; controller box with spring COMMIT button (100 N/m, 8 mm travel) and status lamp. Sockets, modules, button, and contact dynamics are physically simulated with penalty contacts and friction. Status lamp and socket match logic are computed in Python and rendered via kinematic marker write_pose.
